$comment: THE SHARED METRIC FIXTURE (spec P-10, AC-073/AC-074, T-035).
One dataset, two consumers: tests/unit/metric-definitions.test.ts runs the pure functions over
it, and tests/integration/dashboard-filters.test.ts LOADS THE SAME FILE into local Postgres and
runs the canonical SQL fragments over it. Neither suite restates the data, so a fixture edit
moves both results or the parity test fails -- which is exactly the proof AC-074 asks for.
EVERY EXPECTED VALUE BELOW IS HAND-COMPUTED, and the numbers were chosen so that every rate is
exactly representable in binary floating point (denominators 2 and 4, never 3 or 6). A rate of
4/6 would make the 'no tolerance' SQL-vs-pure equality in AC-074 a coin flip on rounding rather
Money is a decimal STRING everywhere, never a JSON number: numeric(18,2) comes back from
node-postgres as a string deliberately (A-12, T-008 money pins) and the metric module does its
money arithmetic on exact scaled integers. Writing 1200.00 as a JSON number here would launder
it through a double before the module ever saw it.
Hand-computed over the period 2026-03-01..2026-03-31 with today = 2026-04-01.
Q5 sits entirely in February and is present ONLY to prove the date window actually excludes;
Q6 is decided-but-EXPIRED and is present ONLY to prove 'decided' means won+lost, not
'has a decision date' (V-091's 'undecided quotes excluded from the win-rate denominator').
